outline.title: Signal from the Deep
outline.premise: In a world drowned by catastrophic flooding decades ago, Maren Voss operates a lonely radio relay station perched atop a half-submerged skyscraper. Her job is to log silence — to confirm that the dead cities below stay dead. When she picks up a coherent broadcast from Valence, a coastal metropolis that sank thirty years ago, she must decide whether the signal is proof of impossible survival, a trap laid by desperate scavengers, or the hallucination of a mind too long alone — and whether chasing it is an act of courage or the final surrender to delusion.
themes: Hope versus delusion — the danger and necessity of believing in the impossible
Isolation as slow erosion of the self
The pull of the impossible as both salvation and destruction

characters.name: Maren Voss
characters.role: Protagonist — solo radio operator at Relay Station Apex
characters.arc: Begins as a woman who has made peace with a world of confirmed losses; ends having risked everything on an unverifiable hope, changed by the act of reaching rather than by what she finds.

characters.name: The Voice
characters.role: Disembodied presence — the broadcaster transmitting from Valence, identity unknown
characters.arc: Exists only as signal and implication; never fully explained, serving as a mirror for Maren's need rather than a character in their own right.

characters.name: Dov Reiss
characters.role: Secondary — Maren's monthly supply runner and only human contact
characters.arc: Starts as a pragmatic anchor to Maren's reality; his failure to return on schedule becomes the crack that lets the signal's pull become irresistible.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.beat: Maren's routine world of catalogued silence is shattered when her equipment locks onto a clear, structured broadcast rising from the coordinates of drowned Valence.
chapters.arc_notes: Act I — Setup: Ordinary world established, inciting incident delivered, first plot point crossed as Maren chooses to respond to the signal rather than log it as interference and move on.

chapters.title: The Frequency of Need
chapters.beat: Maren spends days in obsessive dialogue with The Voice, her certainty of its reality growing even as Dov fails to arrive and her supplies dwindle, until a navigational coordinate embedded in the broadcast forces her to choose between staying safe and sailing toward Valence.
chapters.arc_notes: Act II — Confrontation: Early obstacles and midpoint shift; Dov's absence removes her last anchor to caution, the coordinate transmission reframes the stakes from passive listening to active and dangerous pursuit, and Maren's isolation is revealed as the wound that makes the signal impossible to resist.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.beat: Maren reaches the coordinates above Valence and finds not a living city but a looping automated beacon set by survivors who died years ago — yet she broadcasts her own voice into the deep anyway, planting a signal for anyone still listening, and turns her boat toward an unmapped ridge that may hold higher ground.
chapters.arc_notes: Act III — Resolution: Climax and transformation made visible; the external mystery resolves into ambiguous loss rather than triumph, but Maren's internal arc completes as she chooses to generate hope rather than merely receive it, demonstrating she has moved from passive endurance to active belief.
